name: DTC Returns Abuse Playbook: Fair Tiered Policy with Graduated Responses
short_description: A tiered returns system with structured reasons, photo rules for damage claims, account-level scoring, inspection discipline, and warn-before-restrict workflow.
long_description: This kit helps small DTC sellers handle returns consistently: a tiered policy template with plain language, a case log with scoring formulas for triage, a customer pattern summary at the account level, an inspection log with factual criteria, a denial-with-reason letter and appeal review form, a photo-requirement notice for damage claims, and a monthly tuning sheet that keeps thresholds aligned with logged outcomes. Graduated steps warn before restricting, with appeal preserved throughout.
buyer_persona: Founders and operations or service leads at small DTC apparel, beauty, and similar shops who handle returns with a small team and want consistent fair handling.
problem_statement: Abusive patterns such as wardrobing, empty-box returns, and serial returning drain margin, while blunt crackdowns punish sound customers who need ordinary exchanges.
outcome_statement: A steady routine of structured reasons, evidence, account-level scoring for triage, graduated warn-before-restrict steps, documented appeals, and monthly tuning.
whats_included: Guide with method and checklists, five-sheet workbook with scoring and tuning formulas, tiered policy text, denial letter, appeal form, photo notice.
who_for: Small DTC sellers in fit-sensitive categories with manual or small-team returns handling who want fair consistent steps.
who_not_for: Large retailers with dedicated fraud tooling, sellers seeking automated chargeback software, and sellers needing legal clearance across jurisdictions.
how_to_use: Adopt the reason list, log every case with photos and inspection, score by formula for triage, follow graduated steps with written reasons and appeal, and tune monthly with dated changes.
limitations: Scores prioritize review and do not find abuse alone. Consequential steps require human review of evidence and history. Policy must fit applicable consumer rules and processor terms. No outcome promised.
disclaimer: Operational guidance only. Review policy language against applicable consumer protection rules and processor terms. No outcome promised. Appeal rights stay intact at every restrictive step.
faq: Q: Can a score alone deny a return? A: No, human review with evidence and written reasons plus appeal is required. Q: Are photos needed for every return? A: No, mainly for damage claims and flagged inspections. Q: Do restrictions warn first? A: Yes, graduated steps warn before any narrow time-bound limit. Q: Does this promise loss reduction? A: No, it provides structure and tuning without outcome promises.
keywords: returns policy, abuse prevention, wardrobing, inspection checklist, risk score, denial letter, appeal form, DTC operations
changelog: Version 1.0: initial release with guide, five-sheet workbook, and four templates.
support: Email support for file access and use questions. For legal questions contact counsel. For processor questions contact the provider.
